modules.description: Unified 4-level taxonomy (SentimentState, TransitionType, TrajectoryType, DomainConfig) mapping cross-domain labels to unified closed vocabulary.

Full Model (OET).cross_domain_unification: Yes — unified loss over Amazon and Dravidian domains
Full Model (OET).notes: Single source of truth across all 3 multi-task heads.

mBERT Sentence.cross_domain_unification: Yes for sentiment only; cannot reason over transitions/trajectories
mBERT Sentence.notes: Inherits unified sentiment states from dataset loader, but isolated from sequential ontology.

XLM-R Sentence.cross_domain_unification: Yes for sentiment only; cannot reason over transitions/trajectories
XLM-R Sentence.notes: Same as mBERT sentence; cross-lingual vocabulary benefit at token level only.

LSTM-Only (Ablation).notes: Evaluates sequential trajectory without attention weighting; no transition head.

Attention-Only (Ablation).notes: Attends directly over token embeddings into trajectory head; lacks recurrence.

TextCNN.notes: Non-transformer baseline; utilizes static embeddings mapped to ontology sentiment classes.

modules.description: Pretrained encoder representation quality and domain adaptation fit via Masked Language Modeling perplexity (src/mlm_perplexity_eval.py).

Full Model (OET).params: 180,946,443 total; 177,853,440 frozen encoder; 3,093,003 trainable (BiLSTM 2,828,032 + classifier 199,179 + attention 65,792)
Full Model (OET).notes: Captures subwords for Dravidian code-mixed scripts; perplexity evaluated via MLM evaluation head.

mBERT Sentence.encoder_type: bert-base-multilingual-cased (0 layers trainable -- re-run 2026-09-05 at matched capacity, see docs/capacity_matched_comparison.md; superseded the original 2026-09-04 run's all-12-layers-trainable configuration)
mBERT Sentence.params: 177,853,440 frozen encoder; 198,404 trainable (linear classifier head only, outputs/logs/baseline_mbert_sentence_amazon.json)
mBERT Sentence.notes: Serves as direct comparison for mBERT encoder representation without sequence modeling.

XLM-R Sentence.encoder_type: xlm-roberta-base (SentencePiece 100-language model; 0 layers trainable -- re-run 2026-09-05 at matched capacity, see docs/capacity_matched_comparison.md)
XLM-R Sentence.params: ~278M total encoder (frozen); 198,404 trainable (linear classifier head only, outputs/logs/baseline_xlmr_sentence_amazon.json)
XLM-R Sentence.notes: Larger vocabulary and higher capacity for Dravidian scripts; compared via src/mlm_perplexity_eval.py.

LSTM-Only (Ablation).notes: Shares encoder with full model; differs only by absence of attention mechanism.

Attention-Only (Ablation).notes: Shares encoder with full model; differs only by absence of BiLSTM encoder.

TextCNN.encoder_type: Randomly-initialised nn.Embedding (300d), learned from scratch -- no pretrained vectors
TextCNN.vocab_size: <=20,000 whitespace tokens built from the training split (build_vocab)
TextCNN.notes: Cannot compute MLM perplexity because no masked language model pretraining exists.

modules.module_name: Module 4: Sequential Opinion Modeling, Calibration & SCS
modules.description: Multi-task opinion tracking capabilities: sentiment, pairwise transitions, sequence trajectory, calibration (ECE), entropy, and Sequence Consistency Score (SCS).

Full Model (OET).scs_metric: Supported — calculates temporal prediction consistency across reviews
Full Model (OET).prediction_entropy: Supported (monitored per head: sentiment, trend, trajectory)
Full Model (OET).ece_calibration: Supported — Expected Calibration Error binned over confidence
Full Model (OET).notes: The ONLY model with all 3 classification heads and attention turning-point localization.

mBERT Sentence.trend_head: N/A — independent sentence predictions lack sequence context
mBERT Sentence.scs_metric: N/A — sentence-level model produces no sequence trajectories
mBERT Sentence.notes: Demonstrates performance drop when sequential evolution across reviews is ignored.

XLM-R Sentence.trend_head: N/A — independent sentence predictions lack sequence context
XLM-R Sentence.scs_metric: N/A — sentence-level model produces no sequence trajectories
XLM-R Sentence.notes: Tests whether stronger multilingual representation can compensate for lack of sequence modeling.

LSTM-Only (Ablation).sequential_encoder: Bidirectional LSTM (final hidden state pooled, no attention)
LSTM-Only (Ablation).trend_head: N/A — baseline omitted trend head to isolate trajectory ablation
LSTM-Only (Ablation).scs_metric: Supported — sequential predictions permit SCS computation
LSTM-Only (Ablation).prediction_entropy: Supported for sentiment and trajectory heads
LSTM-Only (Ablation).ece_calibration: Supported for sentiment and trajectory heads
LSTM-Only (Ablation).notes: Ablation model proving the necessity of the Attention mechanism for turning points.

Attention-Only (Ablation).sequential_encoder: Multi-Head Self-Attention directly over embedding sequence (no LSTM)
Attention-Only (Ablation).trend_head: N/A — baseline omitted trend head to isolate trajectory ablation
Attention-Only (Ablation).scs_metric: Supported — sequential predictions permit SCS computation
Attention-Only (Ablation).prediction_entropy: Supported for sentiment and trajectory heads
Attention-Only (Ablation).ece_calibration: Supported for sentiment and trajectory heads
Attention-Only (Ablation).notes: Ablation model proving that attention without recurrent order memory degrades temporal tracking.

TextCNN.notes: Traditional n-gram feature baseline without deep contextualization or temporal tracking.

modules.description: Cross-domain evaluation (Amazon Beauty <-> Dravidian Tamil/Malayalam/Kannada) and fuzzy typicality scoring (src/fuzzy_domain_score.py).

Full Model (OET).transfer_mechanism: Unified ontology states + BiLSTM sequence representations
Full Model (OET).fuzzy_typicality_score: Supported — sequence centroid distance to domain clusters
Full Model (OET).expected_degradation: Moderate — sequence dynamics and attention buffer against domain shifts
Full Model (OET).notes: Full architecture transfers both sentiment vocabulary and temporal trajectory dynamics.

mBERT Sentence.expected_degradation: High — lexical shift between Amazon product reviews and Dravidian comments causes steep drop
mBERT Sentence.notes: Lacks temporal smoothing; vulnerable to localized vocabulary mismatch.

XLM-R Sentence.transfer_mechanism: Direct sentence-level token transfer with 100-language pretraining
XLM-R Sentence.expected_degradation: High to Moderate — slightly better cross-lingual transfer, but still lacks sequential dynamics
XLM-R Sentence.notes: Bigger vocabulary aids Dravidian tokens, but trajectory transfer is impossible.

LSTM-Only (Ablation).expected_degradation: Moderate to High — without attention, early/late review bias exacerbates domain shift
LSTM-Only (Ablation).notes: Shows importance of attention for selectively weighting domain-invariant features.

Attention-Only (Ablation).expected_degradation: Moderate — attention identifies salient tokens, but unordered sequence representations drift
Attention-Only (Ablation).notes: Captures salient keywords across domains, but misses temporal transition structure.

TextCNN.fuzzy_typicality_score: N/A — static embeddings do not align with contextualized centroid space
TextCNN.expected_degradation: Severe — static embeddings suffer from high out-of-vocabulary rates across code-mixed domains
TextCNN.notes: Fails to generalize across code-mixed scripts without subword tokenization.
